e-5613.knowledge_point: Finding an Expression for a Least-Squares Regression Curve
e-5613.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ | $2$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression (in terms of $X$ and $\mathbf{y}$) for the vector of coefficients $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ of the curve $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072333/assets/0329ad2c30d00d6051e2be094d076960d3ecfc35f9054feac195787f3af7328d.png)
e-5613.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
X \boldsymbol{\beta} = \mathbf{y},
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by $X^T,$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
X^T \! X {\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X^T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
{\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} = (X^T \! X )^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}.
$$

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β2x2 that best fits the data.

X=[12221332144215521662],β=[β0β1β2],y=[3−55−40]

a
(XTX)−1XTy
b
XTy

(XXT)−1y
d
X(XTX)−1y

XXTy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β1x+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

Xβ=y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by XT, we obtain the corresponding normal equation

XTXβ^=XTy.

Since the columns of X are linearly independent, the matrix XTX is invertible and

β^=(XTX)−1XTy.

content.knowledge_point: Finding an Expression for a Least-Squares Regression Curve
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-5$ | $5$ | $-4$ | $0$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

decision.explanation: Least squares gives the normal equations X^T Xβ̂=X^T y. The columns of X are independent, since a quadratic vanishing at five distinct x-values must be zero. Thus X^T X is invertible and β̂=(X^T X)^{-1}X^T y, which is option a.

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Submit

EXPLANATION

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β1x+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

Xβ=y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by XT, we obtain the corresponding normal equation

XTXβ^=XTy.

Since the columns of X are linearly independent, the matrix XTX is invertible and

β^=(XTX)−1XTy.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a: the normal equations X^T Xβ̂=X^T y give β̂=(X^T X)^{-1}X^T y because X has independent columns. Option c is invalid: XX^T is singular, and Xy has incompatible dimensions.

content.knowledge_point: Finding an Expression for a Least-Squares Regression Curve
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $0$ | $1$ | $3$ | $-3$ | $2$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & 7 & {7}^{2} \\ 1 & 9 & {9}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

decision.explanation: The least-squares coefficients satisfy X^T Xβ̂=X^T y. Since a nonzero cubic cannot vanish at five distinct x-values, X has independent columns and X^T X is invertible. Therefore β̂=(X^T X)^{-1}X^T y, which is option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β1x+β2x2+β3x3

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

Xβ=y,

β^=(XTX)−1XTy.

x 0 2 4 6 8
y 5 1 0 −3 1

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β2x2 that best fits the data.

X=[10021222144216621882],β=[β0β1β2],y=[510−31]

a
(XTX)−1XXTy
b
XT(XXT)−1y
c
XXT(XXT)−1y
d
X(XTX)−1XTy
e
(XTX)−1XTy
Submit

decision.explanation: The least-squares coefficient vector satisfies X^T Xβ̂=X^T y. The columns of X are independent because a nonzero quadratic cannot vanish at five distinct x-values. Hence X^T X is invertible, giving β̂=(X^T X)^{-1}X^T y, option e. Option d instead gives the five fitted y-values.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$2$** | **$4$** | **$6$** | **$8$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $5$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-3$ | $1$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2} \\ 1 & 8 & {8}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Submit

EXPLANATION

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β1x+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

Xβ=y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by XT, we obtain the corresponding normal equation

XTXβ^=XTy.

Since the columns of X are linearly independent, the matrix XTX is invertible and

β^=(XTX)−1XTy.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that the normal equations X^T Xβ̂=X^T y yield β̂=(X^T X)^{-1}X^T y, option e. X has independent columns, so X^T X is invertible. Option a has incompatible matrix dimensions.

content.knowledge_point: Finding an Expression for a Least-Squares Regression Curve
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$2$** | **$4$** | **$6$** | **$8$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $5$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-3$ | $1$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2} \\ 1 & 8 & {8}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

decision.explanation: The least-squares coefficients satisfy X^T Xβ̂=X^T y. Since a nonzero quadratic cannot vanish at five distinct x-values, X has independent columns, so X^T X is invertible. Therefore β̂=(X^T X)^{-1}X^T y, option a. XX^T is singular, making option d undefined.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** | **$7$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-2$ | $2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $-3$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2} \\ 1 & 7 & {7}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β1x+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

| $y$ | $-2$ | $2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $-3$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2} \\ 1 & 7 & {7}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

?
x 1 2 3 4 5
y −20 −10 40 20 10

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

a
[−20−10402010]
b
[1222324252]
c
[(−20)2(−10)2402202102]
d
[11111]
e
[12345]
Submit

decision.explanation: The observation vector contains the measured y-values in table order: -20, -10, 40, 20, 10. This is option a.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-20$ | $-10$ | $40$ | $20$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-20$ | $-10$ | $40$ | $20$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ -10 \\ 40 \\ 20 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

a
[−20−10402010]
b
[1222324252]
c
[(−20)2(−10)2402202102]
d
[11111]
e
[12345]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION
x 1 2 3 4 5
y −20 −10 40 20 10

The coefficients of the curve

y=β0+β1x+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[11121222133214421552]⏞X[β0β1β2]⏞β=[−20−10402010]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that the observation vector lists the measured y-values in order: -20, -10, 40, 20, 10. Option a matches this vector; option b lists squared x-values from the design matrix.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Elements of a Polynomial Regression Model
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-20$ | $-10$ | $40$ | $20$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-20$ | $-10$ | $40$ | $20$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ -10 \\ 40 \\ 20 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

[β0β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

decision.explanation: The observation vector lists the measured y-values in table order: 1, -2, -1, 4, 5. This is option c.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{2} & {0}^{3} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Elements of a Polynomial Regression Model
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $4$ | $5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{2} & {0}^{3} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 9
?
x −3 −1 1 3 5
y −5 −25 5 20 35

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[−5−3(−3)2−25−1(−1)251122033235552]
b
[1−3(−3)21−1(−1)2111213321552]
c
[−3112−1112111231125112]
d
[1−5(−5)21−25(−25)21552120202135352]
e
[−3−5(−5)2−1−25(−25)21552320202535352]
Submit

decision.explanation: For y=β₀+β₁x+β₂x², each design-matrix row is [1,x,x²]. Substituting x=-3,-1,1,3,5 in table order gives option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $-25$ | $5$ | $20$ | $35$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $-25$ | $5$ | $20$ | $25$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & (-3)^{2} \\ 1 & -1 & (-1)^{2} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -25 \\ 5 \\ 20 \\ 35\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Elements of a Polynomial Regression Model
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $-25$ | $5$ | $20$ | $35$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-3$** | **$-1$** | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $-25$ | $5$ | $20$ | $25$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & (-3)^{2} \\ 1 & -1 & (-1)^{2} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{2} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -25 \\ 5 \\ 20 \\ 35\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 10
?
x 1 2 3 4 5
y 3 −2 −1 1 −1

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β2x2+β3x3 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector y in this context?

a
[3−2−11−1]
b
[131−21−1111−1]
c
[1112131415]
d
[111213122223133233144243155253]
e
[12345]
Submit

decision.explanation: The observation vector contains the measured y-values in table order: 3, -2, -1, 1, -1. This matches option a.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

?
x 0 1 2 3 4
y 15 −13 −5 −4 10

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β1x+β3x3 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β1β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[100203111213122223133233144243]
b
[10031113122313331443]
c
[0020311213222233323344243]
d
[1020311213122231323314243]
e
[10021112122213321442]
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients multiply 1, x, and x³, so each row of X is [1,x,x³]. Using x=0,1,2,3,4 gives option b; no x² column is included because the model has no quadratic term.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $-13$ | $-5$ | $-4$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $-13$ | $-5$ | $-4$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & {0}^{3} \\ 1 & 1 & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -13 \\ -5 \\ -4 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $-13$ | $-5$ | $-4$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 12
?
x 2 3 4 5 6
y −5 2 −3 5 −2

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β0+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β0β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[−52222332−34425552−2662]
b
[222332442552662]
c
[12221332144215521662]
d
[1213141516]
e
[122132142152162]
Submit

decision.explanation: The model y=β₀+β₂x² uses the basis functions 1 and x², so each row of X is [1,x²]. Substituting x=2,3,4,5,6 gives option e.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $2$ | $-3$ | $5$ | $-2$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $2$ | $-3$ | $5$ | $-2$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {2}^{2} \\ 1 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & {6}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$-4$** | **$-2$** | **$0$** | **$2$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-7$ | $10$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $-5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-4$** | **$-2$** | **$0$** | **$2$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-7$ | $10$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $-5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-4 & (-4)^{2} & (-4)^{3} \\ -2 & (-2)^{2} & (-2)^{3} \\ 0 & {0}^{2} & {0}^{3} \\ 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 10 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$-4$** | **$-2$** | **$0$** | **$2$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-7$ | $10$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $-5$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-4$** | **$-2$** | **$0$** | **$2$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-7$ | $10$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $-5$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-4 & (-4)^{2} & (-4)^{3} \\ -2 & (-2)^{2} & (-2)^{3} \\ 0 & {0}^{2} & {0}^{3} \\ 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 10 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 14
?
x 1 3 5 7 9
y −5 0 −1 2 −1

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β1x+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[−512032−152272−192]
b
[112132152172192]
c
[1113151719]
d
[112332552772992]
e
[−5103−1527−19]
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients β₁ and β₂ multiply x and x², so each design-matrix row is [x,x²]. Using x=1,3,5,7,9 gives option d.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} \\ 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 7 & {7}^{2} \\ 9 & {9}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} \\ 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 7 & {7}^{2} \\ 9 & {9}^{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients of the curve y=β1x+β2x2+β3x3 that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

[β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[−511213033233−155253277273−199293]
b
[1121333233552537727399293]

[1121313233152531727319293]

decision.explanation: The model uses x, x², and x³, so each design-matrix row is [x,x²,x³]. Substituting x=1,3,5,7,9 gives option b.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3} \\ 7 & {7}^{2} & {7}^{3} \\ 9 & {9}^{2} & {9}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
content.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$5$** | **$7$** | **$9$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-5$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3} \\ 7 & {7}^{2} & {7}^{3} \\ 9 & {9}^{2} & {9}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.
